note: Business-policy scan lexicon of the finding #24 occurrence ledger (DESIGN.md:863, 872, 874). No entry writes a scanned literal: every literal is matched through the SHA-256 of its normalised key (matchers regex with hashes, window, brand); a regex matcher without hashes is a structural pattern that names no literal. derive/scan.mjs is the normative implementation. Forms: path (the repository-relative path, line 0), raw (each line), token (JavaScript and JSON constant strings with escapes decoded, adjacent constant fragments joined across + on any number of lines and constant template substitutions folded), decoded (markup character references, CSS escapes and percent escapes, also inside JavaScript constants). Matches of one entry are leftmost-longest and never overlap; every match is one occurrence. reviewed (format /3): occurrences of block B sealed expectation files that were reviewed token by token as generic words, published legacy API values or homographs; in strict mode the scanner does not report an occurrence bound by a reviewed record to its exact file (path SHA-256 and file SHA-256) and span; no entry, matcher or hash is removed. relocated (format /4): base ledger rows whose source line a block B edit changed after the base without touching their span, each with the post-base columns and line SHA-256 of the same occurrence (README "Reviewed occurrences", "Relocated base rows"); the integration scan and the probe rescan pair an occurrence with its base row through them, the scanner does not read them, and a relocated row keeps its rule and disposition.

matchers.regex: ECMAScript regular expression applied with the g and d flags (plus flags); group span (default 1) is the occurrence and group keyGroup (default span) the key. With hashes, the key normalised by key must have a listed SHA-256 (fnv1a32 is an optional FNV-1a 32-bit prefilter of the normalised key); without hashes the pattern is structural and every match counts.
matchers.window: Every window of length UTF-16 units, normalised by key (exact or ascii-lower), whose SHA-256 is listed; rk32 is the polynomial rolling-hash prefilter (base 257, modulo 2^32) of the normalised window.
matchers.brand: tests/helpers/brand.mjs#brandTokens with extraHashes; only keeps the tokens whose lower-case SHA-256 is listed; tokens are located at their whole-token, part, word-pair or bracketed positions.

keys.words: every run of whitespace, underscore or hyphen replaced by one space
keys.bracket-lower-words: an optional backslash, the opening bracket and following spaces removed at the start, spaces, an optional backslash and the closing bracket removed at the end, then lower-words
keys.alternation-lower: backslashes removed, ascii-lower, the alternatives split on the vertical bar, sorted and joined by it

contexts: A hashed literal may list contexts; in strict mode it matches only where one context holds: raw {before, after} regular expressions tested immediately before and after the span in a path or raw value, or token whole (the span is a whole constant string). The relaxed mode used on the seal's own files ignores contexts and scopes of hashed matchers.

reviewed.note: Reviewed occurrences of the integration zero-literal scan (README "Reviewed occurrences"). A token is one exact literal (entry and literal SHA-256) of an unmatched occurrence of the tracked tree; it is reviewed only in the eligible files (the block B sealed expectation trees and their clause tables by prefix, other block B files by exact path), and each record binds its occurrences by path SHA-256, file SHA-256 and span, so that any change of a bound file reports them again. Classes: generic-word (a common word or phrase, used with its ordinary meaning or as synthetic data; common in the installed third-party packages of the lockfile), legacy-api-value (a value or name of the published legacy API that the base ledger retains with disposition legacy-api and that a block B legacy adapter case or published-API test must reproduce exactly), homograph (a code or data token of other meaning that coincides with the literal). Business literals are never reviewed: they are removed from the sealed file that carries them. derive/reviewed.mjs computes the bindings and the scan; the seal test checks that every record binds exactly its file's occurrences.

In the block B source src/profile/lot4-export.ts (2 occurrences, one line) it is the key of the request that the lot-4 pre-normalize lint passes to runLintSync and the read of the same-named property of the compileLintPolicy result: the upstream lint settings (rule name to severity and options) of the exported interface LintRunRequest (src/profile/lint-bridge.ts:223, base row I-0960) and of the result type of compileLintPolicy (src/profile/lint-contracts.ts:47, I-0965). Both declarations are byte-identical on main (63a9258), ship in its package declarations (dist/**) and are kept by the base as context-generic rows of rule R-093; a declaration published on main is not renamed.

relocated.note: Relocated base rows of the integration zero-literal scan (README "Reviewed occurrences", "Relocated base rows"). A record continues one base ledger row (row) whose source line a block B edit changed after the base without touching the row's span: line, column, endLine and endColumn give the post-base position of the same occurrence and lineSha256 the SHA-256 of the post-base line; file, form, entry, family, literal, key and the span length are the row's, and rule, category, consumer, targetRef and disposition repeat its classification. edit names the block B commit and every base row of the same base line whose span the edit replaced, with the post-base columns and the SHA-256 of the replacement. The integration scan (derive/reviewed.mjs) and the probe rescan (probe-expectations.json#/probe2/trackedRescan) pair an occurrence with the base row through the record's key exactly as through the row's base key, and a row pairs with one occurrence at most through all its keys. A relocation is not a review: the row keeps its rule, disposition and post-migration obligations, and any change of the post-base line voids the key. No record is current. The three records of the previous seal (RL-01 to RL-03: rows I-1427, I-1462 and I-1464 of src/react/workshop.tsx, edit dc183c2) were retired by the final spec pass: the block B fix of review finding 17 restored their base lines byte for byte, so the three occurrences pair with their base rows through the base key, and a record left in place would pair the renamed lines again; any later edit of these lines is reported by the I1 scan.
